claim: Protein histidine methylation is a rare post-translational modification of unknown biochemical importance.
source: Protein histidine methylation is a rare post-translational modification of unknown biochemical importance.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that characterizes the current state of knowledge about protein histidine methylation.

claim: In vertebrates, only a few methylhistidine-containing proteins have been reported, including β-actin as an essential example.
source: In vertebrates, only a few methylhistidine-containing proteins have been reported, including β-actin as an essential example.
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about the limited number of known methylhistidine-containing proteins in vertebrates.

claim: The evolutionary conserved methylation of β-actin H73 is catalyzed by an as yet unknown histidine N-methyltransferase.
source: The evolutionary conserved methylation of β-actin H73 is catalyzed by an as yet unknown histidine N-methyltransferase.
evidence: This statement describes the state of knowledge prior to the current study, indicating that the enzyme responsible was unknown.

claim: SETD3 is the actin-specific histidine N-methyltransferase.
source: We report here that the protein SETD3 is the actin-specific histidine N-methyltransferase.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by multiple experimental approaches including purification, in vitro assays, and knockout studies.

claim: Recombinant rat SETD3 methylated β-actin at H73 in vitro.
source: In vitro, recombinant rat and human SETD3 methylated β-actin at H73.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro methylation assays using recombinant proteins.

claim: Recombinant human SETD3 methylated β-actin at H73 in vitro.
source: In vitro, recombinant rat and human SETD3 methylated β-actin at H73.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro methylation assays using recombinant proteins.

claim: Knocking-out SETD3 in human HAP1 cells resulted in the absence of methylation at β-actin H73 in vivo.
source: Knocking-out SETD3 in both human HAP1 cells and in Drosophila melanogaster resulted in the absence of methylation at β-actin H73 in vivo
evidence: This claim is supported by CRISPR/Cas9 knockout experiments and mass spectrometry analysis of actin from knockout cells.

claim: Knocking-out SETD3 in Drosophila melanogaster resulted in the absence of methylation at β-actin H73 in vivo.
source: Knocking-out SETD3 in both human HAP1 cells and in Drosophila melanogaster resulted in the absence of methylation at β-actin H73 in vivo
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of SETD3 knockout flies and mass spectrometry of actin.

claim: β-actin from wildtype HAP1 cells was > 90% methylated.
source: whereas β-actin from wildtype cells or flies was > 90% methylated.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis showing the proportion of methylated actin peptides.

claim: β-actin from wildtype Drosophila flies was > 90% methylated.
source: whereas β-actin from wildtype cells or flies was > 90% methylated.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis of actin from wildtype flies.

claim: Setd3-deficient HAP1 cells have less cellular F-actin.
source: As a consequence, we show that Setd3-deficient HAP1 cells have less cellular F-actin and an increased glycolytic phenotype.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy imaging of F-actin in wildtype and knockout cells.

claim: Setd3-deficient HAP1 cells have an increased glycolytic phenotype.
source: As a consequence, we show that Setd3-deficient HAP1 cells have less cellular F-actin and an increased glycolytic phenotype.
evidence: This claim is supported by measurements of glucose consumption and lactate production in knockout cells.

claim: Protein methylation is one of the most common post-translation modifications in eukaryotic cells.
source: Protein methylation is one of the most common post-translation modifications (PTMs) in eukaryotic cells (for a review, see Clarke, 2013)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: Histones are the best studied substrates of protein N-methyltransferases.
source: histones are the best studied substrates of protein N-methyltransferases.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field.

claim: Methylation of lysine and arginine residues in histones plays a fundamental role in the epigenetic control of mammalian gene expression.
source: Consequently, much is known about the methylation of lysine and arginine residues in histones and about the fundamental role of such modifications in the epigenetic control of mammalian gene expression (Greer and Shi, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a published work.

claim: Methylation of non-histone proteins is a prevalent PTM that regulates diverse biological processes, including protein synthesis and signal transduction.
source: In addition, there are a growing number of examples showing that the methylation of non-histone proteins is a prevalent PTM that regulates diverse biological processes, including protein synthesis and signal transduction (for a review, see Biggar and Li, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: Non-histone proteins may be methylated on atypical residues such as glutamate, glutamine, cysteine and histidine.
source: More interestingly, non-histone proteins may be methylated on atypical residues such as glutamate, glutamine, cysteine and histidine (Clarke, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: The methylation of histidine residues in proteins has been known for many years.
source: The methylation of histidine residues in proteins has been known for many years
evidence: This is a statement of historical knowledge in the field.

claim: β-actin contains methylated histidine residues.
source: The methylation of histidine residues in proteins has been known for many years but, curiously, only for a few proteins in Nature, including β-actin (Johnson et al., 1967)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a 1967 publication.

claim: S100A9 protein contains methylated histidine residues.
source: The methylation of histidine residues in proteins has been known for many years but, curiously, only for a few proteins in Nature, including β-actin (Johnson et al., 1967), S100A9 protein (Raftery et al., 1996)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Myosin contains methylated histidine residues.
source: The methylation of histidine residues in proteins has been known for many years but, curiously, only for a few proteins in Nature, including β-actin (Johnson et al., 1967), S100A9 protein (Raftery et al., 1996), myosin (Elzinga and Collins, 1977)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Myosin kinase contains methylated histidine residues.
source: The methylation of histidine residues in proteins has been known for many years but, curiously, only for a few proteins in Nature, including β-actin (Johnson et al., 1967), S100A9 protein (Raftery et al., 1996), myosin (Elzinga and Collins, 1977), myosin kinase (Meyer and Mayr, 1987)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Ribosomal protein RPL3 contains methylated histidine residues.
source: The methylation of histidine residues in proteins has been known for many years but, curiously, only for a few proteins in Nature, including β-actin (Johnson et al., 1967), S100A9 protein (Raftery et al., 1996), myosin (Elzinga and Collins, 1977), myosin kinase (Meyer and Mayr, 1987) and ribosomal protein RPL3 (Webb et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Protein methylation on histidine residues may be a quite common phenomenon, modifying dozens if not hundreds of intracellular proteins in mammalian cells.
source: However, a recent study from Ning et al. (2016) suggests that protein methylation on histidine residues may actually be a quite common phenomenon, modifying dozens if not hundreds of intracellular proteins in mammalian cells.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a 2016 study.

claim: The yeast protein Yil110w (Hpm1p) methylates histidine 243 in the ribosomal protein Rpl3p.
source: The yeast protein Yil110w (Hpm1p), which methylates histidine 243 in the ribosomal protein Rpl3p, is the first and only histidine protein methyltransferase molecularly identified to date (Webb et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Hpm1p is a seven β-strand methyltransferase (7BS MTase).
source: Hpm1p is the seven β-strand methyltransferase (7BS MTase), which has been classified in the methyltransferase family 16 (MTF16) (for review, see Falnes et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a review.

claim: The MTF16 group comprises mostly protein-lysine methyltransferases.
source: The MTF16 group comprises mostly protein-lysine methyltransferases, such as Mettl20–23 and Camkmt, with the noticeable exceptions of Hpm1p and of Efm7, which methylates the N-terminal glycine in the eukaryotic translation elongation factor one alpha (eEF1A).
evidence: This is a statement about the composition of the MTF16 family, based on established knowledge.

claim: The enzyme responsible for actin-specific histidine methylation has been partially purified.
source: On the other hand, the enzyme responsible for actin-specific histidine methylation has been partially purified, but the gene encoding this enzyme remains to be identified (Vijayasarathy and Narasinga Rao, 1987; Raghavan et al., 1992).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Actin is one of the most abundant proteins in eukaryotic cells.
source: Actin is one of the most abundant proteins in eukaryotic cells and a major component of the cytoskeleton (for a review, see Pollard and Cooper, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a review.

claim: Actin is a major component of the cytoskeleton.
source: Actin is one of the most abundant proteins in eukaryotic cells and a major component of the cytoskeleton (for a review, see Pollard and Cooper, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a review.

claim: Actin is a highly conserved protein during evolution (≈90% identity between yeast and human protein).
source: It is a highly conserved protein during evolution (≈90% identity between yeast and human protein)
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about actin conservation.

claim: In vertebrates there are three main actin isoforms that only differ by a few amino acids at their N-terminus.
source: and in vertebrates there are three main isoforms that only differ by a few amino acids at their N-terminus.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about vertebrate actin isoforms.

claim: α-Actins are expressed in skeletal, cardiac and smooth muscle.
source: α-Actins are expressed in skeletal, cardiac and smooth muscle
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about actin isoform expression.

claim: β- and γ-actin isoforms are present in non-muscle and muscle cells.
source: whereas β- and γ-isoforms are present in non-muscle and muscle cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about actin isoform expression.

claim: Under physiological conditions, actin exists as a 42-kDa monomeric globular protein (G-actin) that binds ATP.
source: Under physiological conditions, actin exists as a 42-kDa monomeric globular protein (G-actin) that binds ATP and spontaneously polymerizes into stable filaments (F-actin).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about actin structure and function.

claim: G-actin spontaneously polymerizes into stable filaments (F-actin).
source: Under physiological conditions, actin exists as a 42-kDa monomeric globular protein (G-actin) that binds ATP and spontaneously polymerizes into stable filaments (F-actin).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about actin polymerization.

claim: Once actin filaments have been assembled, the terminal phosphate of the bound ATP is hydrolyzed.
source: Once these filaments have been assembled, the terminal phosphate of the bound ATP is hydrolyzed and slowly released from actin, leading to the sequential depolymerization of the filament.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about actin dynamics.

claim: The maintenance of a pool of actin monomers, the initialization of the polymerization process, and the regulation of the assembly and turnover of actin filaments involve more than 100 interacting partner proteins.
source: The maintenance of a pool of actin monomers, the initialization of the polymerization process, and the regulation of the assembly and turnover of actin filaments are extremely complex and well controlled. These involve more than 100 interacting partner proteins, so that actin contributes to more protein–protein interactions than any other protein (Lappalainen, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Actin contributes to more protein–protein interactions than any other protein.
source: These involve more than 100 interacting partner proteins, so that actin contributes to more protein–protein interactions than any other protein (Lappalainen, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Actin plays a role in cell growth, division, and motility.
source: Actin plays a role in many central cell functions, including cell growth, division, and motility (Dominguez and Holmes, 2011)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Actin is essential for cell survival.
source: which makes it essential for cell survival.
evidence: This is an inference based on the critical roles of actin in cell functions.

claim: H73 methylation stabilizes actin filaments in vitro.
source: As a result, it was shown in vitro that H73 methylation stabilizes actin filaments, and that the rate of filaments depolymerization was increased when actin was non-methylated (Nyman et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The rate of actin filament depolymerization was increased when actin was non-methylated in vitro.
source: As a result, it was shown in vitro that H73 methylation stabilizes actin filaments, and that the rate of filaments depolymerization was increased when actin was non-methylated (Nyman et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: SETD3 was previously shown to act as a histone lysine methyltransferase.
source: We reveal that SETD3 is responsible for the methylation of H73 in human and drosophila actin, and that a loss of SETD3 activity impacts the phenotype of the human HAP1 cell line by lowering F-actin content and increasing glycolytic activity.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study (Eom et al., 2011).

claim: Actin-specific histidine N-methyltransferase activity was purified from rat leg muscle approximately 1200-fold.
source: Following numerous purification steps, the N-methyltransferase activity was purified from rat leg muscle approximately 1200-fold (see Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the purification data presented in Table 1.

claim: The methyltransferase was eluted as a single peak in each of the purification steps.
source: The methyltransferase was eluted as a single peak in each of the purification steps (Figure 1), indicating the presence of a single enzyme species.
evidence: This claim is supported by the chromatography data shown in Figure 1.

claim: No methylation of H73A β-actin was detected at any stage of the purification.
source: No methylation of H73A β-actin was detected at any stage of the purification, suggesting that the myofibrillar extract of rat muscle is devoid of other β-actin-methylating enzymes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the enzymatic assay data throughout the purification.

claim: The overall yield of the purification was about 0.6%.
source: The overall yield of the purification was only about 0.6% (see Table 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by the data in Table 1.

claim: Eighteen peptide sequences from rat SETD3 were identified by MS/MS that covered about 39% of its sequence.
source: Eighteen peptide sequences from the rat SETD3 (underlined in Figure 2) that had shared identity with other SETD3 proteins in the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Protein database were found to cover about 39% of its sequence.
evidence: This claim is supported by the mass spectrometry data and the sequence alignment shown in Figure 2.

claim: SETD3 protein was the only methyltransferase found in fraction 14 of Superdex 200.
source: However, to exclude the possibility of missing any potential methyltransferase as the result of a poor extraction of tryptic peptides from protein bands, we performed the MS/MS identification of all proteins present in the entire fraction 14 of Superdex 200 (see Figure 1B) and fraction F3 of Reactive red 120 (see Figure 1C), and SETD3 protein was again the only methyltransferase found in these fractions.
evidence: This claim is supported by comprehensive mass spectrometry analysis of the purified fractions.

claim: SETD3 protein was the only methyltransferase found in fraction F3 of Reactive red 120.
source: However, to exclude the possibility of missing any potential methyltransferase as the result of a poor extraction of tryptic peptides from protein bands, we performed the MS/MS identification of all proteins present in the entire fraction 14 of Superdex 200 (see Figure 1B) and fraction F3 of Reactive red 120 (see Figure 1C), and SETD3 protein was again the only methyltransferase found in these fractions.
evidence: This claim is supported by comprehensive mass spectrometry analysis of the purified fractions.

claim: Orthologs of SETD3 were found in almost all eukaryotes including vertebrates, insects, plants and fungi.
source: Protein BLAST searches (Altschul et al., 1997) with rat SETD3 and phylogenetic analysis of the resulting sequences indicated that orthologs of this protein were found in almost all eukaryotes including vertebrates (≈75–98% identity with the rat sequence), insects (≈35–40% identity), plants and fungi (≈30% identity) (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by BLAST searches and phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: No SETD3 orthologs were detected in the sequenced proteome of Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
source: No SETD3 orthologs were detected in the sequenced proteome of Saccharomyces cerevisiae or of Naegleria gruberi in agreement with previous reports, showing the absence of actin-specific histidine methyltransferase activity in these species (Kalhor et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by BLAST searches and is consistent with previous reports cited.

claim: No SETD3 orthologs were detected in the sequenced proteome of Naegleria gruberi.
source: No SETD3 orthologs were detected in the sequenced proteome of Saccharomyces cerevisiae or of Naegleria gruberi in agreement with previous reports, showing the absence of actin-specific histidine methyltransferase activity in these species (Kalhor et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by BLAST searches and is consistent with previous reports cited.

claim: All identified SETD3 proteins contain the SET and Rubisco LSMT substrate-binding domains at their N- and C-terminus, respectively.
source: All identified SETD3 proteins contain the SET and Rubisco LSMT substrate-binding domains at their N- and C-terminus, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: The SET domain is thought to interact directly with the protein substrate.
source: The SET domain is thought to interact directly with the protein substrate and most probably contributes indirectly to SAM binding too
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis and established knowledge about SET domains.

claim: The Rubisco LSMT substrate-binding domain seems to interact with a protein substrate only.
source: whereas the Rubisco LSMT substrate-binding domain seems to interact with a protein substrate only (see Figures 2 and 4).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis shown in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: Recombinant rat and human SETD3 catalyzed the methylation of recombinant β-actin, but not of the H73A mutant.
source: The recombinant enzymes catalyzed the methylation of recombinant β-actin, but not of the H73A mutant (see Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro methylation assays shown in Figure 5.

claim: Recombinant human and rat SETD3 produced in COS-7 cells had a specific activity of approximately 5 nmol.min−1.mg−1 protein.
source: Their specific activity was similar to that determined for the enzymes produced in the COS-7 cells (≈5 nmol.min−1.mg−1 protein)
evidence: This claim is supported by enzymatic activity measurements.

claim: Recombinant human and rat SETD3 produced in E. coli had a specific activity similar to that of enzymes produced in COS-7 cells.
source: Their specific activity was similar to that determined for the enzymes produced in the COS-7 cells (≈5 nmol.min−1.mg−1 protein), which further confirms the identification of SETD3 as the actin-specific methyltransferase.
evidence: This claim is supported by enzymatic activity measurements comparing enzymes from different expression systems.

claim: Rat and human SETD3 have a very high affinity towards both SAM and human β-actin.
source: Rat and human SETD3 have a very high affinity towards both SAM and human β-actin (Table 3), with KM values well below the physiological concentrations of SAM and β-actin monomers in vertebrate cells (≈ 30 µM and 50–100 µM, respectively (Clarke and Banfield, 2001; Pollard, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic measurements presented in Table 3 and comparison with physiological concentrations from cited sources.

claim: The KM for β-actin was about 4-fold lower for human SETD3 (≈0.8 µM) than for the rat enzyme (3 µM).
source: Both enzymes had comparable estimates of Vmax value at saturating concentrations of SAM, but the KM for β-actin (≈0.8 µM) was about 4-fold lower for human SETD3 than for the rat enzyme (3 µM).
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic data in Table 3.

claim: The catalytic efficiency (KM/kcat) of human SETD3 towards β-actin was 3-fold higher than that of the rat enzyme.
source: Consequently, the catalytic efficiency (KM/kcat) of human SETD3 towards β-actin was 3-fold higher than that of the rat enzyme (see Table 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic data in Table 3.

claim: Actin peptide H was a very poor substrate for SETD3.
source: By contrast, actin peptide H was a very poor substrate for SETD3 as rat and human SETD3 catalyzed methylation of the peptide with extremely low Vmax values and showed several thousand–fold lower affinity towards the peptide in comparison to the values determined with human β-actin (see Table 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic data in Table 3.

claim: Peptide YPIEHGIVTNWDDMEK containing the H73 residue was the only tri-deuterium-methylated peptide detected by PLGS 2.4 software.
source: Peptide YPIEHGIVTNWDDMEK (M + H = 1963.9355 Da) containing the H73 residue was the only tri-deuterium-methylated peptide detected by the PLGS 2.4 software (Waters, USA).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 9.

claim: Both rat and human SETD3 enzymes catalyzed tri-deuterium-methylation of H73 in β-actin.
source: Both rat and human SETD3 enzymes catalyzed tri-deuterium-methylation of H73 in β-actin
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 9.

claim: No tri-deuterium-methylation was detected in YPIEHGIVTNWDDMEK peptide or in any other tryptic peptide derived from β-actin protein incubated in the absence of SETD3.
source: whereas no such modification was detected in YPIEHGIVTNWDDMEK peptide (M + H = 1946.9021 Da) or in any other tryptic peptide derived from β-actin protein incubated in the absence of SETD3 (see Figure 9).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 9.

claim: SETD3 methylated peptide H at least 10-fold more efficiently than peptide H3N4.
source: We could see that SETD3 methylated both peptides (Figure 8—figure supplement 1), but peptide H was at least 10-fold more efficiently methylated than peptide H3N4, confirming that SETD3 is most probably a histidine N-methyltransferase rather than a lysine-specific methyltransferase.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative methylation assays shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Neither rat nor human SETD3 methylated ATP-β-actin or ADP-β-actin produced in yeast.
source: Surprisingly, neither rat nor human SETD3 methylated ATP-β-actin or ADP-β-actin, as determined using the radiochemical assay (Figure 10, see Figures 6 and 7)
evidence: This claim is supported by methylation assays shown in Figure 10.

claim: Yeast-produced human β-actin became a good substrate for SETD3 when purified in denaturing conditions and re-folded into nucleotide-free quasi-native actin.
source: More importantly, yeast-produced human β-actin became a good substrate for SETD3 when purified in denaturing conditions and re-folded into nucleotide-free quasi-native actin, as did E. coli-produced recombinant human β-actin (see Figure 10).
evidence: This claim is supported by methylation assays shown in Figure 10.

claim: The methylation of profilin-β-actin complex was negligible.
source: The methylation of profilin-β-actin was negligible and that of cofilin-β-actin complex was low (only ≈3–4% of the total protein in the complex could be methylated).
evidence: This claim is supported by methylation assays of actin-binding protein complexes.

claim: The methylation of cofilin-β-actin complex was low (only ≈3–4% of the total protein in the complex could be methylated).
source: The methylation of profilin-β-actin was negligible and that of cofilin-β-actin complex was low (only ≈3–4% of the total protein in the complex could be methylated).
evidence: This claim is supported by methylation assays of actin-binding protein complexes.

claim: Five distinct Setd3-KO clonal HAP1 cell-lines were generated using CRISPR/Cas9 technology.
source: Five distinct Setd3-KO clonal HAP1 cell-lines were generated, as described in the 'Materials and methods', and three of these were ultimately selected for further studies (KO-A1, KO-A3 and KO-A5).
evidence: This claim is supported by the description of the CRISPR/Cas9 methodology and the resulting cell lines.

claim: Methylation of the H73 residue was detected in almost all H73-containing β-actin peptides derived from wildtype HAP1 cells.
source: As shown in Figure 12C, methylation of the H73 residue was detected in almost all H73-containing β-actin peptides derived from the wildtype HAP1 cells
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 12C.

claim: Close to 90% of β-actin peptides derived from two different Setd3-deficient cell lines were not methylated at H73.
source: whereas close to 90% of the same β-actin peptides derived from two different Setd3-deficient cell lines were not methylated at H73.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 12C.

claim: The knock-out of SETD3 in Drosophila prevented the methylation of all three different forms of actin (actin-42A, −57B and −87E) present in extracts from fly larvae.
source: As shown in Table 4, the knock-out of SETD3 prevented the methylation of all three different forms of actin (actin-42A, −57B and −87E) present in extracts from the fly larvae
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Table 4.

claim: All H74-containing actin peptides derived from wildtype Drosophila larvae were methylated.
source: whereas all H74-containing actin peptides derived from wildtype larvae were methylated.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Table 4.

claim: There was a clear decrease in F-actin content in SETD3-KO HAP1 cells.
source: This technique showed a clear decrease in F-actin content in SETD3-KO cells, where actin was largely non-methylated at H73 (Figure 13)
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy imaging shown in Figure 13.

claim: The absence of methylation of H73 destabilized actin in the temperature range between 30°C to 46°C.
source: When cell extracts were heated at increasing temperatures, it became clear that the absence of methylation of H73 destabilized actin in the temperature range between 30°C to 46°C (Figure 14).
evidence: This claim is supported by thermal stability assays shown in Figure 14.

claim: Both the formation of lactate and the consumption of glucose in SETD3-KO cell lines were increased by about 15–20% in comparison with control cells.
source: As shown in Figure 15, both the formation of lactate and the consumption of glucose in SETD3-KO cell lines were increased by about 15–20% in comparison with those determined for the control cells
evidence: This claim is supported by metabolic measurements shown in Figure 15.

claim: SETD3 was originally reported as a methyltransferase that methylates histone H3 at K4 and K36 residues in zebrafish and mouse.
source: SETD3 was originally reported as a methyltransferase that catalyzes the modification of histone H3 at K4 and K36 residues in zebrafish and mouse (Kim et al., 2011; Eom et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous publications.

claim: SETD3 is predominantly localized in the cytosol of human cells.
source: This view was further strengthened by the finding that SETD3 is predominantly localized in the cytosol of human cells, while only a small portion is found in the nucleus (Cheng et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous publication.

claim: The activity of SETD3 with histone peptide H3N4 was at least 4000-fold lower than that with recombinant β-actin.
source: When we investigated the methyltransferase activity of SETD3 with either the actin peptide H or the histone peptide H3N4, however, the activity with the histone peptide was at least a 4000-fold lower than that of recombinant β-actin.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative activity measurements.

claim: The actin preparation used in the study may comprise actin molecules with stable non-native spatial structures.
source: Given that, on the one hand, it is not possible to produce natively folded actin in bacteria (Stemp et al., 2005; Martín-Benito et al., 2002) and that, on the other hand, the ATP/ADP-free actin denatures rapidly and irreversibly (Graceffa and Dominguez, 2003), it is likely that the actin preparation used in our study may comprise actin molecules with stable non-native spatial structures.
evidence: This is an inference based on cited knowledge about bacterial actin production and actin stability.

claim: Only a small portion of the actin monomers produced in bacteria and purified under denaturing conditions adopted a conformation that was recognized by the SETD3 enzyme.
source: This observation was readily reproducible in the presence of bacterial SAH nucleosidase and adenine deaminase, suggesting that it was not due to a potential accumulation of SAH in the reaction mixture (unpublished data, Drozak et al.). This indicates that only a small portion of the actin monomers produced in bacteria and purified under denaturing conditions adopted a conformation that was recognized by the SETD3 enzyme.
evidence: This is an inference based on the substoichiometric methylation observed in the experiments.

claim: Rat and human SETD3 are rather 'lazy' enzymes, with a kcat of 0.6–0.8 min−1.
source: Both tested SETD3 orthologs are rather 'lazy' enzymes, with a kcat of 0.6–0.8 min−1, resembling the values estimated for protein methyltransferases rather than those measured for enzymes catalyzing the methylation of low-molecular-weight substrates (Clarke and Banfield, 2001; Osborne et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic data and comparison with values from cited sources.

claim: The intracellular concentrations of SAM and β-actin monomers in vertebrate cells are about 30 µM and 50–100 µM, respectively.
source: Considering that the intracellular concentrations of SAM and β-actin monomers in vertebrate cells are about 30 µM and 50–100 µM, respectively (Clarke and Banfield, 2001; Pollard, 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published sources.

claim: The presence of ATP or ADP could create a structural hindrance that prevents SETD3 from reaching the H73 residue.
source: This finding may suggest that the presence of ATP or ADP could create a structural hindrance that prevents SETD3 from reaching the H73 residue if the methyltransferase interacts with actin through the nucleotide-binding cleft (see Figure 4).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observation that nucleotide-bound actin is not methylated.

claim: Nucleotide-free actin monomers in a complex with one or more actin-binding proteins of yet unknown identity could be the physiological substrate for the SETD3 methyltransferase.
source: Taken together, these observations have led us to hypothesize that nucleotide-free actin monomers in a complex with one or more actin-binding proteins of yet unknown identity could be the physiological substrate for the SETD3 methyltransferase.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental observations with different forms of actin.

claim: Many SET-domain-containing methyltransferases are found in complexes with numerous other proteins that are essential for their catalytic activity and substrate specificity.
source: Indeed, many of these methyltransferases are found in complexes with numerous other proteins that are essential for their catalytic activity and substrate specificity.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: The yeast histone H3 methyltransferase SET1 requires the presence of seven different proteins that form a complex named COMPASS.
source: For example, to exert its catalytic activity, the yeast histone H3 methyltransferase SET1 requires the presence of seven different proteins that form a complex named COMPASS (Complex of Proteins Associated with Set1), and similar COMPASS-like complexes are formed by other mammalian SET-domain-containing methyltransferases (for a review, see Herz et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: Disruption of SETD3 activity leads to the depletion of F-actin and a loss of cytoskeleton integrity.
source: Our results identify β-actin as a novel substrate of SETD3 and show that disruption of its activity leads to the depletion of F-actin and a loss of cytoskeleton integrity.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 13.

claim: The biochemical role of the methylated H73 residue is likely to contribute to stabilizing the structure of monomers that build the ATP-F-actin.
source: Thus, the biochemical role of the methylated H73 residue is likely to contribute to stabilizing the structure of monomers that build the ATP-F-actin and to delay the intermolecular conformational rearrangements of F-actin that complement the hydrolysis of ATP.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed effects of H73 methylation on actin stability and filament dynamics.

claim: The methylated actin derived from wildtype HAP1 cells is more thermo-stable than the non-methylated one from SETD3-KO cells.
source: This conclusion finds at least partial confirmation in the thermal stability assay, which shows that the methylated actin derived from the wildtype HAP1 cells is clearly more thermo-stable than the non-methylated one (SETD3-KO cells) (see Figure 14).
evidence: This claim is supported by thermal stability assays shown in Figure 14.

claim: The polymerization and depolymerization of actin filaments cause up to 50% of total ATP consumption in vertebrate cells.
source: Both the polymerization and the depolymerization of actin filaments occur continuously even in resting cells and constitute a major energy drain, causing up to 50% of total ATP consumption in vertebrate cells (Kudryashov and Reisler, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: The destabilization that leads to the accelerated degradation of hypomethylated F-actin probably drives an increasing demand for ATP that could be fulfilled by shifting the cell metabolism towards glycolysis.
source: Thus, the destabilization that leads to the accelerated degradation of hypomethylated F-actin probably drives an increasing demand for ATP that could be fulfilled by shifting the cell metabolism towards glycolysis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed metabolic changes in SETD3-KO cells.

claim: The phenotype of Setd3-deficient cells is somewhat similar to that of malignant cells.
source: The phenotype of Setd3-deficient cells is therefore somewhat similar to that of malignant cells, suggesting that SETD3 activity may play a role in suppressing tumor development.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed metabolic phenotype of SETD3-KO cells.

claim: Hypomethylation of actin was observed in rat cells following their transformation with the Src oncogen.
source: Indeed, the hypomethylation of actin was observed in rat cells following their transformation with the Src oncogen (Chiou et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: The enzymatically inactive SET-domain-loss form of SETD3 was shown to function as a dominant-negative mutant, promoting oncogenesis in human cells.
source: Furthermore, the enzymatically inactive SET-domain-loss form of SETD3 was shown to function as a dominant-negative mutant, promoting oncogenesis in human cells (Chen et al., 2013)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: SETD3 is the first protein-histidine methyltransferase to be identified in vertebrates.
source: The SETD3 enzyme is therefore the first protein-histidine methyltransferase to be identified in vertebrates
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the identification of SETD3 as the actin methyltransferase and the lack of previously identified vertebrate histidine methyltransferases.

claim: SETD3 is the first SET-domain-containing enzyme possibly displaying a dual methyltransferase specificity towards both Lys and His residues in proteins.
source: and the first SET-domain-containing enzyme possibly displaying a dual methyltransferase specificity towards both Lys and His residues in proteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the identification of SETD3 as a histidine methyltransferase and previous reports of its lysine methyltransferase activity.

claim: A loss of SETD3 activity in human HAP1 cells induces phenotypic changes resembling those present in cancer cells.
source: and a loss of SETD3 activity in human HAP1 cells induces phenotypic changes resembling those present in cancer cells, suggesting that the hypomethylation of actin might be involved in tumorigenesis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed metabolic phenotype of SETD3-KO cells.

claim: The actin-specific histidine N-methyltransferase corresponded to a ≈70 kDa protein.
source: Moreover, our results were in agreement with previous reports suggesting that the actin-specific histidine N-methyltransferase corresponded to a ≈70 kDa protein (Raghavan et al., 1992).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous report and is consistent with the molecular weight of SETD3.

claim: The specific methylation of the Nτ-position of H73 by actin-specific histidine methyltransferase was previously shown by Raghavan et al. (1992).
source: The specific methylation of the Nτ-position of H73 by actin-specific histidine methyltransferase was previously shown by Raghavan et al. (1992).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous publication.

claim: Recombinant rat SETD3 catalyzes the specific methylation of the H73 residue present in the synthetic peptide corresponding to the nucleotide sensor loop of β-actin.
source: (ii) recombinant rat SETD3 catalyzes the specific methylation of the H73 residue present in both the recombinant β-actin protein and the synthetic peptide corresponding to the nucleotide sensor loop of β-actin
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro methylation assays with peptide substrates.

claim: The methylation of H73 is a highly conserved modification among actins from many different eukaryotes.
source: The methylation of H73 is a highly conserved modification among actins from many different eukaryotes, although it has been found to be absent from the actin of the amoeboflagellate N. gruberi and the yeast S. cerevisiae (Sussman et al., 1984; Nyman et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous publications.

claim: The methylation of H73 is absent from the actin of the amoeboflagellate N. gruberi.
source: The methylation of H73 is a highly conserved modification among actins from many different eukaryotes, although it has been found to be absent from the actin of the amoeboflagellate N. gruberi and the yeast S. cerevisiae (Sussman et al., 1984; Nyman et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous publications.

claim: The methylation of H73 is absent from the actin of the yeast S. cerevisiae.
source: The methylation of H73 is a highly conserved modification among actins from many different eukaryotes, although it has been found to be absent from the actin of the amoeboflagellate N. gruberi and the yeast S. cerevisiae (Sussman et al., 1984; Nyman et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous publications.

claim: Isolated histones are extremely poor substrates for SETD3.
source: In the present study, we have not examined the activity of recombinant SETD3 towards histones because isolated histones are extremely poor substrates (Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous publication.

claim: Actin is the most abundant actin methyltransferase substrate present in the cytoplasm.
source: Consequently, we identified actin as the novel physiological substrate of SETD3, which is present in the cytoplasm and is likely to be the most abundant actin methyltransferase.
evidence: This is an inference based on the high activity of SETD3 towards actin and its cytoplasmic localization.

claim: SETD3 may be a dual methyltransferase able to methylate both the Lys and His residues of other proteins.
source: It is possible however, that SETD3 may also be a dual methyltransferase able to methylate both the Lys and His residues of other proteins, but this still requires in vivo confirmation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential substrate specificity of SETD3.

claim: Rabbit actin methyltransferase methylated only a minor portion (up to 1% protein) of actin inclusion bodies.
source: This observation is in line with a previous report, showing only a minor methylation of actin inclusion bodies (up to 1% protein) by rabbit actin methyltransferase (Raghavan et al., 1992).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous publication.

claim: SETD3 was at least 200-fold less active towards the synthetic peptide H than towards recombinant β-actin.
source: Furthermore, SETD3 was at least 200-fold less active towards the synthetic peptide H, corresponding to the amino acid sequence surrounding the H73, than was recombinant β-actin (see Table 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic data in Table 3.

claim: Structural features of the actin molecule other than the primary sequence of the sensor loop are probably important for its recognition by the actin methyltransferase.
source: This indicated that structural features of the actin molecule other than the primary sequence of the sensor loop are probably important for its recognition by the actin methyltransferase.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that the peptide is a much poorer substrate than the full-length protein.

claim: The enzymes may be fully saturated by substrates and operate at rates that are close to their Vmax in vivo.
source: These observations suggest that the enzymes may be fully saturated by substrates and operate at rates that are close to their Vmax in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of KM values with physiological substrate concentrations.

claim: The recombinant β-actin used in the kinetic studies is certainly not a physiological form of β-actin.
source: It is important to keep in mind, however, that the recombinant β-actin used in the present kinetic studies is certainly not a physiological form of β-actin.
evidence: This is a statement acknowledging a limitation of the experimental system.

claim: The affinity of SETD3 to physiological β-actin remains to be verified.
source: Therefore, the affinity of SETD3 to physiological β-actin remains to be verified.
evidence: This is a statement about future work needed to confirm the findings.

claim: The H73 is present at the surface of the actin monomers and seems to be easily accessed by the methyltransferase.
source: The H73 is present at the surface of the actin monomers and seems to be easily accessed by the methyltransferase.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis of actin shown in Figure 4.

claim: The estimated dimensions of the actin monomer and of the substrate-binding cleft in SETD3 indicate that actin could be accommodated well at the cleft of the methyltransferase.
source: Furthermore, the estimated dimensions of the actin monomer and of the substrate-binding cleft in SETD3 indicate that actin could be accommodated well at the cleft of the methyltransferase and that steric hindrance should not prevent interactions between these proteins.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: Yeast Yil110w protein methylates His243 of the ribosomal Rpl3 protein only when Rpl3 is associated with the ribosome.
source: If so, this resembles the activity of the yeast Yil110w protein, the only other known protein histidine N-methyltransferase, which methylates His243 of the ribosomal Rpl3 protein only when Rpl3 is associated with the ribosome (Webb et al., 2010; Al-Hadid et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous publications.

claim: SETD3 has been reported to play a role in the regulation of the cell cycle and apoptosis.
source: Several reports describing the role of SETD3 in the regulation of the cell cycle and apoptosis (Kim et al., 2011)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: SETD3 has been reported to play a role in myocyte differentiation.
source: Several reports describing the role of SETD3 in the regulation of the cell cycle and apoptosis (Kim et al., 2011), myocyte differentiation (Eom et al., 2011)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: SETD3 has been reported to play a role in cell response to hypoxic conditions.
source: Several reports describing the role of SETD3 in the regulation of the cell cycle and apoptosis (Kim et al., 2011), myocyte differentiation (Eom et al., 2011), cell response to hypoxic conditions (Cohn et al., 2016)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: SETD3 has been reported to play a role in tumorigenesis.
source: Several reports describing the role of SETD3 in the regulation of the cell cycle and apoptosis (Kim et al., 2011), myocyte differentiation (Eom et al., 2011), cell response to hypoxic conditions (Cohn et al., 2016) and tumorigenesis (Pires-Luís et al., 2015; Cheng et al., 2017) have been published to date.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: Some studies identified the methylation of histones as a primary mechanism of SETD3 action.
source: Some of these studies identified the methylation of histones as a primary mechanism of SETD3 action (Kim et al., 2011; Eom et al., 2011)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: Some studies suggested that SETD3 may modify non-histone substrates that are present in the cytosol.
source: whereas others suggested that the enzyme may instead modify non-histone substrates that are present in the cytosol (Chen et al., 2013; Cohn et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: The existence of two distinct domains in SETD3 has been suggested to be the structural basis for dual substrate specificity.
source: The existence of two distinct domains in SETD3, i.e. SET and Rubisco LSMT substrate-binding domains, has been suggested to be the structural basis for such dual substrate specificity (Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: The phenotype identified in Setd3-deficient human HAP-1 cells is caused by the absence of the catalytic activity of SETD3.
source: Taken together, our results show that the phenotype that we have identified in Setd3-deficient human HAP-1 cells is caused by the absence of the catalytic activity of SETD3, rather than by a non-catalytic or actin-stabilizing interaction between SETD3 and actin filaments.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental results showing loss of actin methylation and phenotypic changes in SETD3-KO cells.

claim: The inherent instability of F-actin in Setd3-deficient HAP1 cells is likely to be at the origin of the increased lactate production by these cells.
source: The inherent instability of F-actin in Setd3-deficient HAP1 cells is likely to be at the origin of the increased lactate production by these cells.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the observed F-actin instability with the metabolic phenotype.
